To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the solar-system test rules out many designer f(R), in particular those that have been widely studied in the literature; (2) the cosmological test rules out many of the designer f(R) and the fine-tuning problem exists for the rest of them; (3) we found that a class of f(R) models, the so-called chameleon f(R) models are consistent with both the solar-system and cosmological tests.

(1) the solar-system test rules out the w = -1 cosmologically distinct designer f(R) model and (2) the cosmological test rules out the designer f(R) cosmologically distinct models with the fine-tuning problem.

(1) the solar-system test of f(R) gravity ruled out the designer f(R) model which is cosmologically different from the ΛCDΜ model and (2) the designer f(R ) model which passes the solar-system test suffers a fine-tuning about the choice of initial condition.

the cosmological and astrophysical implications of modified gravity.

the f(R) gravity is not favored by the solar-system test, and the cosmological tests are not able to distinguish the ΛCDM from many of the f(R)-models.
the cosmological constant is still the most natural explanation of dark energy.
the designer f(R) model is not viable in the sense of being ruled out by both the cosmological and solar-system tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the designer f(R) model is not a good candidate of dark energy.
the designer f(R) model with a w = -1 cosmology, which is frequently studied in the literature, is disfavored both in the cosmological and solar-system tests.
the designer models are not viable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is difficult to find a designer f(R) model which is both cosmologically and solar-systems viable.
it is important to take into account the constraints from the solar-system test when constructing a cosmologically viable f(R) model.
the cosmological and solar-system tests are complementary to each other.
